questions.text: Are the capabilities this business needs in order to run — commercial, delivery or technical, and financial — covered by someone with the competence to do them?

A.text: Significant capabilities the business needs are not covered by anyone

B.text: Capabilities are covered by whoever is available, regardless of whether they are competent in them

C.text: The business has identified the capabilities it needs, and most are covered by someone competent — whether an owner, employee, contractor, adviser, or outsourced provider

D.text: All identified critical capabilities are covered by someone demonstrably competent, and remaining gaps are recognised and being addressed

E.text: As D, and coverage is reviewed as the business changes, so newly critical capabilities are identified before they become gaps

questions.text: Is it clear who is responsible for what, and who is accountable for outcomes?

A.text: Responsibilities are unclear or overlap in ways that cause things to be missed

B.text: Responsibilities are understood informally but not defined; accountability is ambiguous when something goes wrong

C.text: Responsibilities are defined and understood by those involved

D.text: As C, and named individuals are accountable for defined outcomes, not only for activities

E.text: As D, and accountability is exercised in practice — outcomes are reviewed with the accountable person on a defined cycle

questions.text: If a person central to the business became unavailable, how well could the business continue?

A.text: Critical knowledge and relationships sit with one person, undocumented and untransferable; the business would substantially stop

B.text: The dependency is recognised, but nothing has been done about it

C.text: Some critical knowledge and relationships are documented or shared, so parts of the business could continue

D.text: Critical knowledge, relationships and access are documented or shared such that the business could continue operating through an absence

E.text: As D, and this has been tested rather than assumed — through a planned absence, a handover, or another person demonstrably picking up a critical function

questions.text: How are significant decisions made in the business?

A.text: Decisions are made reactively, without information gathered for the purpose

B.text: Decisions are made by whoever is available at the time, on judgement alone

C.text: Significant decisions are made by identified people, using relevant information gathered beforehand

D.text: As C, and significant decisions are recorded with their reasoning, so they can be revisited

E.text: As D, and the business reviews how past significant decisions turned out and adjusts how it makes them

questions.text: Do the people the business depends on stay, and does their capability keep pace with what the business needs?

A.text: People central to the business leave unexpectedly, or capability gaps persist without being addressed

B.text: People generally stay, but capability development is not considered

C.text: The people the business depends on are stable, and capability needs are recognised when they arise

D.text: As C, and capability is deliberately developed — training, mentoring, structured experience, or bringing in expertise

E.text: As D, and development is planned against where the business is going, not only what it needs today
